findings.title: Recovery codes passed in wrong UserCredentialModel field
findings.body: Line 123 builds `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` which puts the JSON list into the `value` field. Federated validators/readers for recovery codes expect the payload in `challengeResponse` (as used by `UserCredentialModel.buildFromBackupAuthnCode`, and by the test provider at `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`/`isValid` which call `input.getChallengeResponse()`). The OTP path in the same file correctly uses `getValue()`, proving the two credential types use different fields. Consequence: a user-storage provider reading `getChallengeResponse()` receives null, stores null/corrupt credentialData and validation fails or NPEs, so creation in user storage is broken.

findings.title: getCredentials NPE for users not in storage map
findings.body: `getCredentials` does `var myUser = getMyUser(user)` then immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check, while every other method in the same class (`isConfiguredFor`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isValid`) guards `myUser == null`. `getCredentials` is invoked via federated-credential streams even for users that are not owned by this provider. Consequence: NullPointerException when listing federated credentials for any non-storage or unknown user, breaking credential listing / login flows.

findings.title: Exhausted recovery codes not removed when stored in user storage
findings.body: After successful validation the code fetches the credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` which now can return a federated (user-storage) credential, but cleanup unconditionally calls `removeStoredCredentialById`. That API only removes local DB credentials and is a no-op for federated credentials, which must be removed/disabled via the storage provider (`disableCredentialType`/`updateCredential`). Consequence: when recovery codes live in user storage and all codes are used, the exhausted credential is never deleted from the external storage, leaving stale state.
